## Laptop Comparison for Video Editing Under $1,500

A is the best all-around fit if you want strong performance and portability within budget. B is the most powerful for editing, while C is the best value and lightest option.

## Ranked Scorecard and Visual Comparison

| Rank | Model | Price | RAM | SSD | CPU | Screen | Battery | Weight | Score |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | B | $1,449 | 32 GB | 1 TB | 10-core | 15-inch | 7h | 1.8 kg | 92 |
| 2 | A | $1,299 | 16 GB | 512 GB | 8-core | 14-inch | 10h | 1.4 kg | 78 |
| 3 | C | $1,099 | 16 GB | 1 TB | 6-core | 13-inch | 12h | 1.3 kg | 72 |

### Simple scorecard
- **B — 92/100**: Best editing performance, strongest multitasking, largest SSD, still under budget
- **A — 78/100**: Balanced choice with good portability and battery life
- **C — 72/100**: Best for travel and storage, but weakest CPU for editing

## Best Pick for Video Editing

### **Model B**
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/laptop.svg
- **Why it wins:** 32 GB RAM and a 10-core CPU make it best for timeline scrubbing, effects, and multitasking.
- **Storage:** 1 TB SSD is ideal for large media files and project caches.
- **Trade-off:** Heavier and shorter battery life than A or C, but still the strongest editing machine under $1,500.

### Best value alternative: **Model A**
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/laptop.svg
- Good if you want a more portable machine with better battery life.
- Enough power for lighter-to-moderate editing.
- Less future-proof than B because of 16 GB RAM and 512 GB SSD.

### Budget-friendly alternative: **Model C**
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/laptop.svg
- Best battery life and lightest weight.
- 1 TB SSD is excellent for media storage.
- CPU is the main limitation for serious video editing.
